title: Room amenities are recorded but never displayed anywhere
description: Raised by the Product Owner while specifying LODGY-69's 'view description'. Confirmed in code, and the gap is wider than 'hard to find': Room.amenities is captured on the room form and the bulk-add form, stored on the entity, carried through RoomRepository.create/update - and then read back by nothing. A grep for 'amenities' across app/src/main/java returns hits in exactly two UI files, RoomFormScreen and BulkRoomFormScreen, and in both it is an editable input rather than a display. There is no read-only surface at all: not the room list, not the bed grid, not All rooms, not the printable PDF packet (LODGY-45), not the monthly report CSV. THE PRACTICAL EFFECT: the only way to read what a room has is to open its EDIT form. So a warden answering 'does 204 have an attached bathroom?' has to enter a screen whose entire purpose is changing things, where a stray keystroke silently edits the record they came to read. That is the actual defect - not that the field is hidden, but that reading it requires entering an editing context. The data itself is safe - it is in the DB and rides along in the backup zip - so this is a display gap, not data loss. SCOPE NOTE: LODGY-69's 'view description' sheet is one place this should surface, but it must not be the ONLY place, or amenities stay invisible to anyone who never taps a bed. The room list and the printable packet are the two that matter most - the packet especially, since it is the document a warden hands to someone, and a room description without its amenities is a thin record. WORTH THE PO's VIEW: amenities is a free-text String today, so it is whatever the warden typed - 'AC, attached bath' or 'ac attached bathroom wifi'. Displaying it is straightforward; making it filterable ('show me rooms with AC') would need it structured as tags, which is a larger change and deliberately NOT in this ticket's scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Room amenities are visible on at least one read-only surface, so reading them never requires opening the edit form
Amenities appear on the room's own detail view, alongside type and price per bed
Amenities appear in the printable PDF packet's room information, since that is the record a warden hands over
A room with no amenities recorded renders cleanly - no empty label, stray separator or blank row
Long free-text amenities wrap or truncate gracefully rather than breaking the layout they appear in
Existing installs need no migration and no re-entry - whatever is already stored displays as typed
The amenities field on the room and bulk-add forms is unchanged; this ticket only adds places to read it

history.note: Filed after the PO flagged that amenities are recorded but not viewable. Verified in code: the only two UI references are the write forms, and there is no read-only surface anywhere including the PDF packet and CSV export. Split out of LODGY-69 so amenities do not end up visible solely inside a bed sheet.
DECIDED: amenities stay free text. No move to structured tags, so no filtering by amenity is planned - the display work here will not be redone later. Scope is display only, as written.
Starting. Adding read-only surfaces for amenities: the bed grid header (the room detail view a warden actually opens) and the printable PDF packet.

Built. Amenities now have two read-only homes, deliberately not just the LODGY-69 bed sheet, since that would leave them invisible to anyone who never taps a bed. (1) The bed grid - the screen a warden opens to look at a room - now shows price per bed and, when recorded, an 'Amenities: ...' line above the bed tiles. (2) The printable PDF packet carries an Amenities row per tenancy, which matters because that is the document handed to someone. A room with nothing recorded renders nothing at all - no empty label, no stray separator - in both surfaces. The forms are untouched; this only adds places to read. VERIFIED ON DEVICE: opened Room 101, which had no amenities, and saw only the price; added 'AC, attached bath' through the edit form; reopened the room from the room list and the amenities line was there. So the original complaint - that the only way to read them was to enter a screen whose purpose is changing them - is resolved. Note for QA: I removed a DUPLICATE room_price_per_bed string that already existed at line 68 and which I had unknowingly re-added; the build caught it as a resource merge error. The surviving definition is the original. TESTS: 2 new in DataPacketTest, one asserting amenities appear and one asserting no line is emitted when blank. Full suite 436 pass, coverage 97.00% line. Not schema-affecting - Room.amenities already existed and is unchanged.
